Published version of the pollinator-competition/floral-resource study; no focal plant antagonist/exploiter response is measured.
Broad pollinator-decline review focuses pollination loss and ecosystem consequences rather than a plant pollinator–antagonist trait geometry.
Impatiens capensis thesis/programme includes simulated pollinator decline, floral-trait selection and herbivory context; retain and resolve report dependence with SCHPRISMA-000723 at full text.
Focused review on pollinator parasites and floral evolution addresses parasites acting through pollinator behaviour, not a focal plant antagonist/exploiter response to the floral coordinate.
Silene pollinator-sharing study concerns reproductive isolation and pollinator overlap without a focal plant antagonist/exploiter channel.
Fritillaria camouflage study measures pollination and reproductive success but does not directly measure herbivore/antagonist response to the focal floral phenotype.
Aeschynanthus dissertation on pollinator shifts, floral evolution and speciation lacks a focal plant antagonist/exploiter response.
Duplicate/alternate repository identity of the Aeschynanthus pollinator-shift dissertation; no focal plant antagonist/exploiter response.
Fuchsia floral-colour-phase study measures pollinator visitation only, without a focal plant antagonist/exploiter response.
Drypetes floral volatile/pollination/fruit-production study lacks a focal plant antagonist/exploiter response.

Arabidopsis lyrata thesis programme experimentally quantifies pollinator-mediated selection and herbivory-associated selection on flowering phenology and floral display across populations/years; retain for same-programme multi-agent adjudication.
Silene latifolia study examines post-pollination floral-scent downregulation in a nursery-pollinator seed-predator system; retain for coupled pollination/seed-predation signal-cost adjudication.
Pre-meeting conference notice/programme on plant–pollinator interactions is not an independent primary study or focused synthesis suitable for the systematic evidence count.
Wolbachia distribution study concerns host ecological contact in animals and has no focal plant floral trait/reward coordinate.
Perspective on pollinator declines and floral evolution focuses pollinator-mediated evolutionary responses without a focal plant antagonist/exploiter response.

Primary Geranium sylvaticum study measures flower size/phenology, pollinator preference, floral herbivory, seed predation and sex-specific seed production across populations; retain for multi-agent selection/context adjudication.
Sequential flower-retention study focuses internal fruit/resource effects on flower abscission and does not measure a pollinator response/service to the focal floral coordinate.
Vochysia study tests protection by a nectar-thieving ant through simulated-herbivore removal; pollinator costs are hypothesized but not measured in the focal experiment.
Silene stellata thesis quantifies context-dependent outcomes of interaction with Hadena ectypa, a pollinating seed predator; retain for nursery-pollination benefit-cost adjudication.

Primary Pedicularis rex experiment manipulates water-filled cupulate bracts and measures legitimate pollinators, nectar robbers, seed predators and seed production; retain as a strong shared-trait mutualist-antagonist candidate.
Carnivorous-pitcher-plant scent comparison addresses floral pollination versus prey-capture function, but does not measure a focal plant antagonist/exploiter response.
Real-time scent-visualization methods study measures emission dynamics without ecological pollinator and antagonist responses.
Pitcairnia floral-visitor study quantifies pollination effectiveness but lacks a focal plant antagonist/exploiter response.
Bromeliad reproductive-biology/flower-visitor study measures pollination and reproductive success but does not establish a focal plant antagonist/exploiter response.
